caption: A square-free number is its own square-free part
Negative $n$: the sign is a unit, so the part is positive
Simplifying $\sqrt{1000}=10\sqrt{10}$: the radicand left over is the square-free part
The part is always square-free. See [[IsSquareFree]]
Zero is outside the domain, so it stays unevaluated
wolfram.note: Wolfram's FactorInteger[0] is {{0, 1}}, which the mapping reads as 0; we leave it unevaluated, as the domain is the nonzero integers.
sage.note: Sage's squarefree_part of 0 is 0; ours leaves it unevaluated, as the domain is the nonzero integers.
